punchline: Sethi's pitch is that the money should be moved by the 7th without you deciding anything, because willpower is the part that fails.
thirty_sec: Ramit Sethi says saving is not about willpower. In his example the paycheck lands on the 1st, the 401(k) share is withheld, and automatic transfers go to savings and a Roth IRA on the 5th, with bills paid by autopay on the 7th. He cites a study where switching 401(k) enrollment from opt-in to opt-out lifted participation from under 40 to nearly 100 percent. What remains in checking is yours to spend.
